steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Demand: P↓->Qd↑ (law); Determinants: income, tastes, related goods, expectations, #buyers

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Supply: P↑->Qs↑; Determinants: input prices, technology, expectations, #sellers, taxes/subsidies

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Equilibrium: Qd=Qs; Shortage: P<P* -> Qd>Qs; Surplus: P>P* -> Qs>Qd

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: PED = %DeltaQd/%DeltaP; elastic (>1), inelastic (<1), unitary (=1); factors: substitutes, necessity, time, %income

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: A monopolist faces demand P = 100 - 2Q and has MC = 20. Find profit-maximising output, price, and profit --- Solution: MR = 100 - 4Q. Set MR = MC: 100 - 4Q = 20 -> Q = 20. P = 100 - 2(20) = 60. Profit = (P - ATC)Q. ATC = TC/Q. If TC = 20Q + 100, ATC = 20 + 5 = 25. Profit = (60-25)x20 = 700

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: If PED = -0.5 and price rises 10%, %DeltaQd? | Explain why monopolies produce less than PC | Calculate CS at P=50, Q=100 for linear demand P=100-Q

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of microeconomics and markets with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: A monopolist faces demand P = 100 - 2Q and has MC = 20. Find profit-maximising output, price, and profit. Solution: MR = 100 - 4Q. Set MR = MC: 100 - 4Q = 20 -> Q = 20. P = 100 - 2(20) = 60. Profit = (P - ATC)Q. ATC = TC/Q. If TC = 20Q + 100, ATC = 20 + 5 = 25. Profit = (60-25)x20 = 700 Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.

steps.title: Homework
steps.body: If PED = -0.5 and price rises 10%, %DeltaQd? Explain why monopolies produce less than PC Calculate CS at P=50, Q=100 for linear demand P=100-Q Evaluate minimum wage using monopsony model Why is PES more elastic in long run?
